createSetupIntent, savePaymentMethod and purchaseSessionPack indeed carry no @RateLimited or other throttle in this file, but the finding's verification caveat (no filter/proxy-level limit in SecurityConfiguration or gateway config; RateLimitingAspect is annotation-driven only) depends on files not provided, so absence of any rate limit cannot be confirmed from this code alone.

getOrCreateStripeCustomer saves the new paymentMethodId over the existing stripe_customers row before paymentGateway.chargeAndCapture, and since purchasePack is non-transactional that save commits immediately in its own default Spring Data transaction. On a failed charge the exception propagates with no restore — previousCard is only read in scheduleSubscriptionCardSync on the success path — so the dead card stays the saved default that later charges read (per the file's own comment "the charge reads it from stripe_customers").
